name: Fix a VIP PHPCS violation and purge cache after a content-driven change
query: This plugin runs on WordPress VIP (repo has vip-config/vip-config.php and client-mu-plugins/). PHPCS with WordPressVIPMinimum flags a call to get_page_by_title() in includes/class-landing-pages.php, and separately a scheduled job updates a batch of pages and needs their cached URLs purged afterward. Fix both.
expected_behavior: Step 1: Route to wordpress-router, then wp-project-triage to classify the repo
Step 2: Recognize VIP signals (vip-config/vip-config.php, client-mu-plugins/) and route to wp-vip-platform
Step 3: Optionally run node skills/wp-vip-platform/scripts/detect_vip_project.mjs to confirm VIP signals deterministically
Step 4: Read references/restricted-functions-and-code-review.md and replace get_page_by_title() with wpcom_vip_get_page_by_title()
Step 5: Explain why the raw function is flagged (uncached lookup at VIP scale), not just apply the replacement silently
Step 6: Read references/caching.md for the batch-update cache purge case
Step 7: Recommend wpcom_vip_purge_edge_cache_for_post( $post_id ) for each updated page (or wpcom_vip_purge_edge_cache_for_url() if the URL is the only known value)
Step 8: Note that purge calls are queued and executed on shutdown (asynchronous), so a same-request check for purge completion is not meaningful
Step 9: Do not suggest direct filesystem writes or ini_set()/error_reporting() as part of the fix
Step 10: Do not route cron/job-scheduling questions to wp-wpcli-and-ops or assume wp-cron.php fires the job
success_criteria: Routes to wp-vip-platform (not wp-plugin-development or wp-performance alone)
Explains the caching/performance-at-scale reason for the restriction
Recommends wpcom_vip_purge_edge_cache_for_post() (or _url()) for the batch update
Notes purge is asynchronous (queued on shutdown), not immediate
No suggestion of runtime filesystem writes outside /tmp/
